ignore any note in the Plan about a restricted shell; that applies to a different runner,
not you. Do not read or follow dev/transformations/*/loop.toml — it belongs to that other
orchestrator (CodeScribe) and has nothing to do with this run.

truth for this phase; evals/tools/archive_experiment.py is the deterministic layer it calls. Do not reimplement
either one — changes to them take effect here automatically.

Everything below is what evals/archive.toml cannot know: the Claude-specific facts about this run.

- groups processed this run: 1

[
  {
    "groupIndex": 1,
    "group": "Group 1: Mods — infrastructure modules (mark TRANSLATED per Spec coverage map)",
    "opened": true,
    "units": [
      "software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.f",
      "software/mcfm/src/Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.f",
      "software/mcfm/src/Mods/Modules_Interface.f90",
      "software/mcfm/src/Mods/pp_mod.f90",
      "software/mcfm/src/Mods/ppwp2j_mod.f90"
    ],
    "authored": [
      {
        "unit": "software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.f",
        "done": "yes",
        "notes": "Created ONE new file: /home/user/JSS-2026-Example/software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.hpp (guard TYPES_MOD, `namespace types_mod`, g++ -fsyntax-only clean). No .cpp, no _fi shim, no CMakeLists edit, nothing moved to deprecated/.\n\nWHY the shape differs from the triage note (\".hpp + .cpp + types_mod_fi.f90 via c_f_pointer, swap CMake entry, move original to deprecated/\"): `module types` declares only four real KIND parameters (sp/dp/ex/qp = selected_real_kind(6/15/18/33)) and zero variables. There is nothing for c_f_pointer to mirror and nothing for extern \"C\" to expose, so a .cpp/_fi pair would be empty scaffolding. This matches the folder's own precedent for parameter-only modules — blabels_mod, heldefs_mod, constants_mod, mxpart_mod, zeta_mod all have .f90 + .hpp and no .cpp.\n\nThe header deliberately declares no names. `selected_real_kind(N)` is compiler-evaluated; the kind integers (gfortran 4/8/10/16) are nowhere in the source, so emitting `const int dp = 8;` would invent values, and C++ has no kind system for them to select in. The precision is already carried at each use site by the Spec's own rule (`real(dp)` -> `double`, `complex(dp)` -> `std::complex<double>`), which is why every already-rewritten header in src/Mods comments out `#include <types.hpp>` and drops `using namespace types`, and why no translated file in the tree includes a types header. The .hpp also settles the roadmap entry (build_roadmap.py counts a file translated when a sibling .cpp OR .hpp exists).\n\n*** LOAD-BEARING FOR INTEGRATE — do NOT swap or delete the `types_mod.f` line in Mods/CMakeLists.txt, and do NOT move types_mod.f into Mods/deprecated/. *** 166 live Fortran files under src/ (grep -rlE '^[[:space:]]*use +types' excluding deprecated/working/gpt-4o-conversions) still `use types` for their real(dp)/complex(dp) declarations. Dropping it from the build breaks all of them at once. The source is mirrored, not obsolete, so the Spec's deprecated-move precondition is not met; the .hpp needs no CMake entry (that file lists only .f/.f90/.cpp). Integrate should have zero build-wiring work for this unit.\n\nExpected status once the restored build passes: TRANSLATED (Mods = infrastructure, no coverage process per Spec coverage map). Ran `python3 dev/workflow.py draft` first as the Plan requires; its output (dev/tmp/drafts/Mods/types_mod.scribe) is a mechanical mis-render (\"int, parameter  dp = selected_real_kind(15)\") and was not used."
      },
      {
        "unit": "software/mcfm/src/Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.f",
        "done": "yes",
        "notes": "Pure binding module: no variables, no own procedures — all 22 names are exported by the external QCDLoop lib (lib/qcdloop-2.0.5/src/wrapper.cc, non-underscore QL_NAMES block). Wrote software/mcfm/src/Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.hpp (extern \"C\" at global scope = true C boundary per Spec rule 6) and software/mcfm/src/Mods/mod_qcdloop_c.f90 (free-form, module name unchanged, all 22 bind(C) interfaces preserved verbatim); git mv'd the original to software/mcfm/src/Mods/deprecated/mod_qcdloop_c.f.\n\nNo .cpp: nothing to define (no state, no procedures), matching other stateless Mods modules (constants_mod, blabels_mod, maxd_mod, zeta_mod = .f90+.hpp only). Hence no _init/_finalize, so Modules_Interface.f90 (a sibling unit this round) needs no edit from me.\n\nSignatures were read off wrapper.cc, not guessed; Fortran bind(C) without value passes by reference so params are const&. Quad entries (qli1q/2q/3q/4q, qli1qc/2qc/3qc/4qc) intentionally omitted from the .hpp: they need real128/__float128, whose only C++ spelling is ql::qcomplex from qcdloop/types.h, and that include dir is NOT on objlib's include path. No C++ caller uses them; their only callers (src/gghgg_dep/Inc/fillformfactor_qp_inc.f, hgggg_integralfillqp_inc.f) are Fortran and reach them unchanged via the module. Nothing dropped.\n\nChecks, all in mktemp -d, no project build, no tests, no CMakeLists touched: gfortran -fsyntax-only on the .f90 passes; sorted-set diff of bind(C,name=) old vs new is empty (22/22); a synthetic `use mod_qcdloop_c` caller compiles against the new .mod; g++ -fsyntax-only on a TU including BOTH mod_qcdloop_c.hpp and src/loop/Loop.hpp passes. That last one was the real hazard — Loop.hpp already declares qli2/qli2c/qli3/qli3c extern \"C\" at global scope, and duplicate C-linkage decls must have identical type; I matched its const& style exactly. Did not edit Loop.hpp (another dir's shared header).\n\nINTEGRATE ACTION: src/Mods/CMakeLists.txt line 2 must swap mod_qcdloop_c.f -> mod_qcdloop_c.f90. Build will not configure until then, since the .f now lives in deprecated/ (expected per Plan step 5). Status should be TRANSLATED once the restored build passes (Mods = infrastructure, no coverage probe).\n\nREVIEW FLAG: named the Fortran file mod_qcdloop_c.f90, not _fi.f90. Spec Output shape says _fi.f90 for modules, but it also says follow existing rewritten modules in src/Mods, where every translated module keeps <modulename>.f90 (_fi is used in src/loop for subroutine translations, which define no module). Module name mod_qcdloop_c is unchanged either way for the 8 existing `use` sites; only the filename is at stake. Rename is trivial if the reviewer prefers _fi."
      },
      {
        "unit": "software/mcfm/src/Mods/Modules_Interface.f90",
        "done": "deferred",
        "notes": "Dependency not ready: all 120 callees lack a C binding. Modules_Interface.f90 is not a module and declares no data — it is two free bind(C) subroutines (modules_fi_init_ / modules_fi_finalize_) that exist only so src/BLHA/CXX_Interface.cxx (decls at lines 35-36, calls at 171/175) can drive Fortran-side pointer binding. It is already the _fi shim for the whole Mods layer, so there is no C++ content to extract into a .hpp/.cpp pair. Verified via `grep -n \"_mod_init.*bind(C\\|_mod_finalize.*bind(C\" *.f90` in src/Mods: zero hits — every <mod>_mod_init/<mod>_mod_finalize is a plain Fortran module procedure reachable only through `use`. Per Spec (\"If a needed module dependency has no usable C binding yet, stop and rewrite that dependency first\" + \"Never invent a called symbol\"), emitting a .cpp would require either adding bind(C) to ~60 sibling _mod.f90 shims (other units, out of scope for this author) or fabricating gfortran-mangled names like __b0_mod_MOD_b0_mod_init in extern \"C\". The Draft output at dev/tmp/drafts/Mods/Modules_Interface.scribe confirms this: it emitted 60 #include <*_mod.hpp> + using-namespace lines but left every `call <mod>_mod_init()` as raw Fortran because no C++ callee exists. Trap 5 is not the blocker — the headers exist, the callable entry points do not. Also still load-bearing: 38 non-Mods Fortran files use masses_mod alone, so the pointer binding cannot be retired. Suggest this unit be reclassified as terminal Fortran glue for the translate step and handled by the cleanup step once no Fortran consumer of the Mods shims remains. No files created, moved, or edited; no build or tests run; CMakeLists.txt untouched; `git status --porcelain software/mcfm/src/Mods/` is clean."
      },
      {
        "unit": "software/mcfm/src/Mods/pp_mod.f90",
        "done": "yes",
        "notes": "Authored pp_mod.hpp + pp_mod.cpp and rewrote pp_mod.f90 in place as the c_f_pointer interface module (the src/Mods convention; no _fi.f90 exists there and CMakeLists already lists pp_mod.f90). Original preserved at src/Mods/deprecated/pp_mod.f90 (already present and byte-identical; verified by diff before editing, nothing moved).\n\nEquivalence checked without touching the project build: compiled the original module and the new C++/shim pair as two standalone drivers in /tmp and diffed a dump of all 6561 entries plus ppmax. Output identical — all 80 nonzeros at identical (i,j,k,l), sum 3240, ppmax=80. Covers traps 3 and 4. Both TUs pass -fsyntax-only (g++ -std=c++11, gfortran). Data was extracted from the source programmatically, not retyped; 6561 values, nonzeros are exactly a permutation of 1..80.\n\nINTEGRATE MUST DO TWO THINGS (I was forbidden to touch either shared file):\n1. src/Mods/CMakeLists.txt — add `pp_mod.cpp` after the existing `pp_mod.f90` entry (line 94). pp_mod.f90 is already listed.\n2. src/Mods/Modules_Interface.f90 — add `use pp_mod, only: pp_mod_init` + `call pp_mod_init()` to modules_fi_init, and the matching pp_mod_finalize to modules_fi_finalize. WITHOUT THIS the Fortran `pp` pointer stays null and software/mcfm/src/Z2jet/qqb_z2jetx_new.f (the only caller, via `use pp_mod`) dereferences null — a silent segfault, spec trap 9. The same file also needs the sibling ppwp2j_mod entries.\n\nShared-header defect noted, not fixed (not my file): FArray4D's pointer constructor in src/Inc/FArray.hpp takes only three extents and self-initializes `nl(nl)` from an indeterminate value. I avoided it by using the allocating 4-extent constructor plus a static copy from pp_data at static-init time (pp is defined before the copy in the same TU, so ordering is defined). g++ -Wall emits only pre-existing -Wreorder warnings from FArray.hpp itself.\n\n`include 'ppmax.f'` retained in the Fortran module (callers get ppmax through `use pp_mod`); on the C++ side pp_mod.hpp includes ppmax_mod.hpp and re-exports it with a using-directive inside namespace pp_mod, matching the precedent in blha_mod.hpp. Dropped `use types` (nothing needs dp; the caller has its own `use types`) and omitted the useless leaking `allocate(...)` that ewcharge/mqq/msq_cs init routines carry.\n\nSibling ppwp2j_mod converged on the same design independently (same FArray4D extents/lower bounds, same accessor naming, same public list). Kept separate, not merged, per triage.\n\nStatus still needs the restored build to pass before it can be logged TRANSLATED (Mods = infrastructure, no coverage per the Spec coverage map); I did not run jobrunner."
      },
      {
        "unit": "software/mcfm/src/Mods/ppwp2j_mod.f90",
        "done": "yes",
        "notes": "Translated to ppwp2j_mod.hpp + ppwp2j_mod.cpp + c_f_pointer shim in ppwp2j_mod.f90, following the ewcharge_mod/msq_cs_mod pattern in src/Mods. Original was already byte-identical in src/Mods/deprecated/ppwp2j_mod.f90, so no move was needed. No symbol invented; .cpp includes its own header; no forward declarations. Verified offline: g++ -std=c++11 -fsyntax-only and gfortran -fsyntax-only both clean, and a /tmp-only link of the new .cpp+shim reproduced all 72 non-zero pp(i,j,k,l) entries and ppmax=80 byte-identically against the original Fortran module (confirms column-major reshape order and -4:4 bounds).\n\nTWO ITEMS FOR THE SERIAL INTEGRATE STEP (I was forbidden to touch either shared file):\n1. software/mcfm/src/Mods/CMakeLists.txt line 95: keep ppwp2j_mod.f90 and add ppwp2j_mod.cpp next to it (same f90+cpp pairing used for ewcharge_mod/msq_cs_mod).\n2. software/mcfm/src/Mods/Modules_Interface.f90 MUST gain `use ppwp2j_mod, only: ppwp2j_mod_init` + `call ppwp2j_mod_init()` in modules_fi_init, and the matching finalize pair. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the sole consumer src/W2jet/qqb_wp2jetx_new.f does `use ppwp2j_mod` and indexes pp(...) directly, so without the init call the shim pointer stays null and W2jet dereferences null -> silent segfault (Spec trap 9), which still builds cleanly. Note pp_mod.f90 in this same round needs its own entry in the same file, which is why I left it alone.\n\nCoverage: Mods is infrastructure per the Spec coverage map, so no @coverage-probe was added (no existing Mods .cpp has one) -> expected status TRANSLATED once the restored build passes."
      }
    ],
    "integrated": [
      {
        "unit": "software/mcfm/src/Mods/types_mod.f",
        "status": "TRANSLATED",
        "notes": "Mirrored by types_mod.hpp (namespace types_mod, no names — selected_real_kind values are compiler-chosen and would be invented). Deliberately KEPT in Mods/CMakeLists.txt and NOT moved to deprecated/: 166 live Fortran files under src/ still `use types`. Compiled as types_mod.f.o. Mods is infrastructure per Spec coverage map, so no coverage probe applies and VERIFIED is unavailable."
      },

        "notes": "Integrate swapped CMakeLists line 2 mod_qcdloop_c.f -> mod_qcdloop_c.f90; original now in Mods/deprecated/. Compiled as mod_qcdloop_c.f90.o. bind(C,name=) set verified identical 22/22 old vs new. Reviewer point for a human: file is named mod_qcdloop_c.f90, not _fi.f90 — Spec Output shape says _fi.f90 for modules but also says follow existing src/Mods modules, which all keep <modulename>.f90; module name is unchanged so the 8 `use` sites are unaffected and a rename is a one-line CMake change."

Both pp_mod.f90.o and pp_mod.cpp.o built; Zjj bench cases all print PASSED, so no silent segfault. No coverage probe (Mods = infrastructure)."
      },

Both ppwp2j_mod.f90.o and ppwp2j_mod.cpp.o built; W+jj and W-jj bench cases all print PASSED. No coverage probe (Mods = infrastructure)."

- create-transformation: This skill should be used when the user asks to "create a transformation", "scaffold a transformation", "add a CodeScribe transformation", "new dev/transformations step", "set up a CodeScribe loop", or otherwise wants to author the plain-file definition of a settle-unit-by-unit code transformation that a CodeScribe loop (or equivalent runner) executes. Produces the folder desired_spec.md + current_plan.md + loop.toml + approvals.toml under dev/transformations/<name>/.
- transform: Run review groups of a dev/transformations/<name> step until the approval gate blocks: continue an open group or open new ones (subject to the gate), author units in parallel, integrate and verify them serially, escalate failures, and record everything in agent_log.md. Loops across groups until the gate blocks or work runs out. Transformation-agnostic — every rule comes from that step's own desired_spec.md and current_plan.md, never from this script. - Point it at any folder under dev/transformations/ via args:{transformation:"mcfm-translate"|"mcfm-cleanup"|"pepper-kokkos-port"|...}. Loops across groups until the approval gate blocks (dev/tools/approve/check_gate.py). After the gate blocks, a human runs approve_group.py then re-invokes. Optional: scope, maxUnits, bundleSize, fixRounds, model overrides.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

def drop_excluded_paths_from_worktree(repo: Path, excludes: list[str]) -> None:
    for path in excludes:
        run(["git", "restore", "--staged", "--worktree", "--", path], cwd=repo, check=False)
        run(["git", "clean", "-fd", "--", path], cwd=repo, check=False)


def validate_session_logs(path_str: str) -> Path:
    """Checked before anything is written, so a bad path leaves no partial archive."""
    path = Path(path_str).expanduser().resolve()
    if not sorted(path.glob("subagents/workflows/wf_*")):
        raise SystemExit(f"no workflow logs under {path}/subagents/workflows/wf_*")
    return path


def copy_session_logs(session_dir: Path, archive_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Flatten a session's out-of-repo logs into the layout evals/analysis reads:
    parse_ccworkflow.py wants <run>/workflow-wf_<id>/{journal.jsonl,agent-*.jsonl}."""
    for wf_dir in sorted(session_dir.glob("subagents/workflows/wf_*")):
        copy_tree(wf_dir, archive_dir / f"workflow-{wf_dir.name}")
    for script in sorted(session_dir.glob("workflows/scripts/*.js")):
        copy_file(script, archive_dir / script.name)


def copy_loop_artifacts(loop_dir: Path, archive_dir: Path) -> None:
    if loop_dir.name == ".claude":
        return  # tracked in git; this run's real artifacts come from --session-logs

    files = [
        "logs/toolusage.toml",
        "loop/run.toml",
        "loop/author.toml",
        "loop/review.toml",
        "loop/review_output.toml",
        "loop/state.toml",
    ]
    for rel in files:
        src = loop_dir / rel
        if src.exists():
            copy_file(src, archive_dir / rel)

    metadata = loop_dir / "loop" / "metadata"
    if metadata.exists() and metadata.is_dir():
        copy_tree(metadata, archive_dir / "loop" / "metadata")


def commit_submodule(repo: Path, branch: str, message: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    action = create_or_checkout_branch(repo, branch)
    excludes = submodule_excludes(repo)
    run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=repo)
    drop_excluded_paths_from_worktree(repo, excludes)
    status = run(["git", "status", "--short"], cwd=repo).stdout.strip()
    info: dict[str, object] = {
        "repo": str(repo.relative_to(ROOT)),
        "branch": current_branch(repo),
        "branch_action": action,
        "excluded_paths": excludes,
        "committed": False,
    }
    if not status:
        info["note"] = "nothing to commit"
        return info
    run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=repo)
    info["committed"] = True
    info["head"] = run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=repo).stdout.strip()
    return info


def write_summary(
    archive_dir: Path,
    experiment_name: str,
    loop_dir: Path,
    transformation_dir: Path,
    submodules: list[Path],
    branch: str,
    submodule_results: list[dict[str, object]],
    included_dev_tmp: bool,
    cleanup_performed: bool,
    session_logs: Path | None,
) -> None:
    summary = {
        "experiment_name": experiment_name,
        "archive_created_at": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "loop_source": str(loop_dir.relative_to(ROOT)),
        "transformation_source": str(transformation_dir.relative_to(ROOT)),
        "submodules": [str(path.relative_to(ROOT)) for path in submodules],
        "archive_branch": branch,
        "submodule_results": submodule_results,
        "session_logs": str(session_logs) if session_logs else None,
        "included_dev_tmp": included_dev_tmp,
        "cleanup_performed": cleanup_performed,
    }
    (archive_dir / "archive_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Deterministic archive tool for eval experiments.")
    parser.add_argument("experiment_name", help="user-provided experiment name")
    parser.add_argument("--transformation", required=True, help="path like dev/transformations/<name>")
    parser.add_argument("--loop-dir", required=True, help="path like .csloop or .codescribe")
    parser.add_argument("--submodule", action="append", default=[], help="path like software/<name>; may be repeated")
    parser.add_argument("--session-logs", help="agent session log dir to archive, for harnesses that log outside the repo")
    parser.add_argument("--include-dev-tmp", action="store_true", help="copy dev/tmp into archive")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    experiment = slugify(args.experiment_name)
    transformation_dir = validate_relative_dir(args.transformation, "dev/transformations")
    loop_dir = validate_relative_dir(args.loop_dir, ".")
    if loop_dir.name not in {".claude", ".csloop", ".codescribe"}:
        raise SystemExit("--loop-dir must point to .claude, .csloop, or .codescribe")
    submodules = [validate_relative_dir(path, "software") for path in args.submodule]

    # evals/analysis finds runs by globbing ccworkflow-*; a mismatched name parses as zero
    # rows rather than failing, so the prefix is enforced here instead.
    if loop_dir.name == ".claude" and not experiment.startswith("ccworkflow-"):
        raise SystemExit(f"a .claude experiment name must start with 'ccworkflow-' (got: {experiment})")
    session_logs = validate_session_logs(args.session_logs) if args.session_logs else None

    date_dir = dt.datetime.now().strftime("%m-%d-%Y")
    archive_dir = ROOT / "evals" / "experiments" / date_dir / experiment
    archive_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    copy_tree(transformation_dir, archive_dir / transformation_dir.relative_to(ROOT))
    copy_loop_artifacts(loop_dir, archive_dir)
    if session_logs:
        copy_session_logs(session_logs, archive_dir)
    if args.include_dev_tmp:
        dev_tmp = ROOT / "dev" / "tmp"
        if dev_tmp.exists() and dev_tmp.is_dir():
            copy_tree(dev_tmp, archive_dir / "dev" / "tmp")
    snapshot_git_context(archive_dir)

    branch = f"evals/{date_dir}/{experiment}"
    submodule_results: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for submodule in submodules:
        if not (submodule / ".git").exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"submodule is not a git repo: {submodule.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        submodule_results.append(commit_submodule(submodule, branch, f"Archive experiment {experiment}"))

    clean_path(ROOT, transformation_dir.relative_to(ROOT))
    # Only clean ephemeral harness directories (.csloop, .codescribe).
    # .claude is tracked by git and should not be cleaned after archiving.
    if loop_dir.name != ".claude":
        clean_path(ROOT, loop_dir.relative_to(ROOT))
    cleanup_performed = True

    write_summary(
        archive_dir,
        experiment,
        loop_dir,
        transformation_dir,
        submodules,
        branch,
        submodule_results,
        args.include_dev_tmp,
        cleanup_performed,
        session_logs,
    )

    print(f"Archived experiment to {archive_dir.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    for result in submodule_results:
        if result.get("committed"):
            print(f"{result['repo']}: on {result['branch']}, committed {result['head']}")
        else:
            print(f"{result['repo']}: on {result['branch']}, {result['note']}")
    print(f"Cleaned {transformation_dir.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    if loop_dir.name != ".claude":
        print(f"Cleaned {loop_dir.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
